From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2026 09:33:10 -0700
Subject: Internal: helion7b-us-east 504 spikes — initial triage

Jasmine / Vanessa — quick triage notes (internal):

Observations:
- Autoscaler churn observed between 08:44–09:06 ET: several workers in the helion7b pool restarted and rejoined.
- Connection backlog on the inference frontends spiked; load balancer started returning 504s once backlog > 4k connections.
- Kernel rollout (quant-optimized backend) pushed at 07:50 ET to a subset of nodes; those nodes show elevated GPU memory pressure and delayed response times.

Likely cause (prelim): the quant-optimized runtime path introduced an edge-case where a new kernel combined with memory growth under specific seq-len caused worker slowdowns; autoscaler then attempted to replace slow workers, creating a brief capacity hole that manifested as 504s.

Immediate mitigations performed (09:18–09:30 ET):
- Rolled back the new kernel on the affected pool (reverted to last-known-good runtime).
- Increased connection queue threshold on frontends to reduce premature 504s while nodes recovered.
- Opened emergency fallback: route ~15% of traffic to helion7b-compact to lower steady-state pressure.

Attachments: autoscaler-metrics-0929.csv (sample metrics window), small trace snippets included inline.

Next steps:
- Continue monitoring (30m), assess error-rate trend.
- Postmortem: capture kernel change details and create rollback checklist for future rollouts.
- Recommend scheduling a deeper reproduction test for quant path with long sequence workloads.

I'll keep you posted; current error rate dropped from ~12% to ~1.2% after the rollback and partial fallback.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin

Hi Jim — quick update from the team (see Marcus' notes below, pasted for context).

TL;DR: We've identified a recent kernel rollout to the quant-optimized path as the likely trigger. We rolled back the kernel and added a temporary partial fallback to helion7b-compact; error rates fell from ~12% to ~1–2%.

What we did (executed between 09:18–09:30 ET):
- Reverted quant kernel rollout on helion7b-v2 in us-east.
- Increased frontend queue threshold to avoid fast 504s during worker recovery.
- Routed 15% of your traffic to helion7b-compact to reduce load on vulnerable workers.

Current status: production latency is near baseline for most traffic; we're continuing to monitor through your peak window. Marcus will follow up with a full RCA and postmortem document.

Action for BluePeak: can you confirm whether you continue to see timeouts on your side for the next 30 minutes? If you notice any lingering issues please send request ids and timestamps and we'll correlate.

Sorry again for the disruption — we'll share a full postmortem once the RCA is complete.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Account Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Helion7b incident (Sep 29) — recovery confirmation and next steps

Hi Jim — following up with closure and next steps.

Summary:
- Incident window: 2026-09-29 08:50–09:30 ET.
- Symptom: elevated 504 gateway/timeouts affecting ~12% of requests at peak.
- Root cause (summary): an automated kernel rollout to the quant-optimized path introduced a memory-growth edge-case under long-sequence traffic that increased worker response times; autoscaler churn created a brief capacity hole.
- Mitigations: rollback of the kernel, increased frontend queue thresholds, and a temporary routing fallback to helion7b-compact. Error rate returned to normal (~0.5–1%).

What we're doing next:
1) Formal postmortem (JIRA INFRA-7123) with repro steps and timeline (owner: Marcus).
2) Add rollout guardrails: require staged-canary with synthetic long-seq test before kernel promotions (owner: Runtime Team).
3) Offer BluePeak: a 10% service credit for the impacted hour window, or a one-time performance tuning session (let me know preference; HubSpot ref: contact-9843).

Attachments & artifacts: helion7b-trace-20260929.log, autoscaler-metrics-0929.csv, helion7b-rollback-notes-0929.txt.

Please let me know if you'd like a short call to walk through the timeline — Vanessa can coordinate. Thanks again for the quick reports and patience while we remediated.

Regards,
